content:
Hi, everyone!

With the release of our stepwise proving system, Real-Prover, we’re introducing reap, yet another lightweight Lean 4 tactic that helps you draft formal proofs one step at a time. reap wraps a premise‑selection service and an LLM into a minimal, composable interface so you can (a) get ranked, parse‑checked next‑move suggestions, (b) click to apply them in VS Code’s Infoview, and (c) extend the pipeline with your own implementation.

  • Blog: https://frenzymath.com/blog/reap
  • Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20613
  • Github: https://github.com/frenzymath/reap

Features

  • Three entry points:
    • reap — pick and apply a good next tactic step.
    • reap! — apply a step only if it solves the goal; otherwise fail.
    • reap? — list clickable suggestions (with proof‑state previews) in Infoview.
  • Infoview widget: a “Try this” panel with colored status: :tada:/green = closes the goal; blue = valid step; gray = invalid.

We are planning to provide public available service for backend inference. Stay tuned!

Development

This implementation is intented to be lightweight and modular with minimal dependency. We also manage to abstract 2 customized wheels for this task:

  1. requests: An requests library for Lean 4 (built on top of curl), it is very basic and can serve the purpose of sending HTTP requests (POST and GET supported), communicating with a local server, etc.

  2. openai_client: An OpenAI-compatible library for Lean 4, it is built on top of the requests library and provides a simple interface to interact with any LLM with an OpenAI-compatible interface. This should be able to reuse in any LLM-related project.

Hope these small implementations can make a better development experience for you. We are also open to contributions and improvements.
